The goal was to present a benchmark system for comparison for which all mathematical operations are described in detail [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the goal was to present a benchmark system for comparison for which all mathematical operations are described in detail. The evidence (Source [S1] passages) explicitly contains the sentence: 'The goal was to present a benchmark system for comparison for which all mathematical operations are described in detail.' However, the rest of the claim lists specific technical implementation details (distributing data using MPI, scattering adjacent tetrahedra, restoring ordering with a global kd-tree, clustering cells, interleaving scan-lines). While these details are present in the evidence, they are attributed to the work of 'Ma and Crockett [Ma97]' and are described as methods used by them, not as the definition of the 'goal' of the benchmark system mentioned in the first sentence. The first sentence refers to a different context (likely the HIAC system or the general benchmark setup), while the subsequent sentences describe Ma and Crockett's specific approach. Therefore, the claim conflates the stated goal of one system with the implementation details of another system described in the same source. Since the specific technical details are not the 'goal' but rather the method of a different cited work, and the claim implies these details define the goal or are part of the same statement's truth value without distinction, it is partially supported (the goal statement is supported, but the attribution of the technical details to that specific goal/context is incorrect or at least distinct in the source).
